items.title: AgentGuard – a QA engine that sits between AI coding agents and LLMs
items.raw_excerpt:
AI coding agents are great at generating code, but terrible at respecting architecture.
We kept getting code that looked correct but didn’t type-check, had hallucinated imports,
or ignored project boundaries. AgentGuard is an open-source quality-assurance engine that sits between an AI coding agent
and the LLM. It enforces a top-down generation pipeline: Skeleton → Contracts → Wiring → Logic Each stage constrains the next, and we validate syntax, imports, linting and types before
any human sees the code. The LLM also self-reviews its output against explicit criteria. AgentGuard supports MCP (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline) and tracks token cost
per model and run. Python 3.11+, MIT licensed.

items.title: Discussion: What would an AI government look like?
items.raw_excerpt: I haven't really heard anyone bring up this topic, so I thought I'd open a discussion here. To me the appeals are obvious. AI governments could theoretically be incorruptible, tireless, consistent, and capable of processing vastly more information than human bureaucracies. They wouldn't accept bribes, play favorites for personal gain, or make decisions based on re-election anxiety. Policy could be optimized across decades rather than election cycles. Practically, I don't know how it would work. What do people here think?

items.title: Vigil – Zero-dependency safety guardrails for AI agent tool calls
items.raw_excerpt: We run 15 AI agents on a production server with full shell access. One of them tried to rm -rf a directory it shouldn't have touched. Another started curling cloud metadata endpoints. We wrote some hardcoded rules to catch the obvious stuff, then realized we were building the same safety layer everyone else will need too. So we extracted it into a library. Vigil is a deterministic rule engine that inspects AI agent tool calls before they execute. 22 rules across 8 threat categories: destructive shell commands, SSRF, path traversal, SQL injection, data exfiltration, prompt injection, encoded payloads, and credential exposure. It's not an LLM wrapper — we don't trust an LLM to guard another LLM. Pure pattern matching, zero dependencies, npm install vigil-agent-safety import { checkAction } f

Vigil is a deterministic rule engine that inspects AI agent tool calls before they execute. 22 rules across 8 threat categories: destructive shell commands, SSRF, path traversal, SQL injection, data exfiltration, prompt injection, encoded payloads, and credential exposure. Over the past three years, AI applications have continuously "broken through" from the lab to everyday life. Whether it's the stunning debut of ChatGPT, the impressive launch of DeepSeek, or tools like Cursor and Lovable enabling entrepreneurs with no coding background to build products, and even Clawbot evolving from concept to usability, the changes in this wave of AI applications are being amplified. However, to date, AI primarily addresses efficiency issues, leaving a truly blank space for another, more challenging question: as tools become increasingly powerful, how should I navigate the rest of my life?  

Against this backdrop, the emergence of the AI application NOOK stands out as somewhat different. On NOOK's interface, users enter their birth time, location, and gender, after which NOOK's proprietary numerical system performs a cold-start profile. Then, an AI called Life Copilot proactively recommends goals and tasks to users—ranging from weight loss and skill acquisition to career planning and personal growth.  

What NOOK aims to achieve is the second stage of AI applications—evolving from efficiency tools to life operating systems. These goals are not left at an abstract level but are broken down into actionable daily tasks.

A Cloud's telemarketing team has been fully integrated into the public cloud team. Recently, A Cloud's telemarketing team underwent a major restructuring, with the previously independent telemarketing team now merged into the public cloud team. Following this integration, reporting lines have also changed; the head of the telemarketing team now reports to the head of the public cloud division. Within A Cloud, telemarketing holds a pivotal position, having once generated over 10 billion yuan in revenue. At its peak, the team comprised more than 1,000 employees across locations such as Hangzhou, Dalian, and Xi'an, a scale rare among cloud service providers. Many may wonder how telemarketing, typically focused on mid- to long-tail clients, could achieve such substantial revenue. In reality, this cloud provider's telemarketing team serves numerous high-value clients with accounts worth millions or tens of millions, which is the core reason it can support billions in revenue. One month prior to this organizational adjustment, the head of the public cloud division was promoted to P12.

Universe Cloud aims to increase its MaaS revenue by at least fivefold by 2026. In 2025, Universe Cloud's leadership had already driven sales efforts for MaaS and higher-level AI tool products through performance metrics tied to large models. Recientemente, el equipo de ventas telefónicas de A Cloud experimentó un importante ajuste: el equipo independiente de ventas telefónicas se ha incorporado al equipo de nube pública. Con esta integración, la estructura de reportes también ha cambiado; ahora el responsable del equipo de ventas telefónicas reporta al director de la división de nube pública.
